enriched.summary: A aula aborda aspectos de gramática, vocabulário e pronúncia, com foco no uso de frases no presente contínuo para explicar situações ou consequências. Também explora palavras e expressões úteis para o dia a dia e como aplicá-las em contextos práticos.
mainTopics: Uso do presente contínuo para explicações e consequências

vocabulary.definition: Used to indicate a reason or cause for something.
examples: I missed the bus because of this.
The meeting was canceled because of this.
He is a kind man.
The man is waiting for the bus.

vocabulary.definition: Plural form of 'man', referring to multiple adult male humans.
examples: Men are stronger together.
The men are playing football.

vocabulary.definition: Refers to Monday through Friday, excluding weekends.
examples: I work on weekdays.
On weekdays, we start school at 8 a.m.

vocabulary.definition: Refers to activities or services provided after a sale.
examples: The company offers postsale support.
Postsale services are important for customer satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: Used to introduce a contrasting idea despite the previous statement.
examples: The weather was bad; even so, we went hiking.
I was tired; even so, I finished my homework.

vocabulary.definition: Happening every day or relating to every day.
examples: I read the newspaper daily.
Daily exercise is important for health.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being new, unusual, or different.
examples: The novelty of the idea attracted investors.
This gadget is no longer a novelty.

vocabulary.definition: Covered with or saturated by water or another liquid.
examples: The ground is wet after the rain.
My clothes got wet at the beach.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to assess and initiate things independently.
examples: She showed great initiative in solving the problem.
Taking initiative is important in leadership roles.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of uncertainty or lack of conviction.
examples: I have no doubt about his honesty.
She expressed doubt about the plan.

vocabulary.definition: An occurrence or happening, especially one of significance.
examples: The event was well-organized.
A major event in history is the moon landing.

vocabulary.definition: The basic cause or source of something.
examples: The root of the problem is poor communication.
She traced the root of the issue.

vocabulary.definition: Used to explain the reason for something.
examples: I stayed home because it was raining.
She is happy because she passed the exam.

grammar.topic: Present Continuous for explanations and consequences
grammar.explanation: The present continuous is used to express actions happening at the moment or temporary situations.
rules: Can be used for both positive and negative sentences.
examples: Don't ask me to sit next to Noah. I'm avoiding contact with him.
I can't participate in the project. I'm finishing another campaign.
Please don't make so much noise. I'm studying. The baby is sleeping.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to use 'to be' before the verb.
Using the base form of the verb instead of '-ing'.

expressions.usage: Used to describe things happening one after another without interruption.
examples: I’ve worked three nights in a row.
They’ve won five games in a row.

practiceQuestions.question: Complete with the correct form of the present continuous: 'The baby _____ (sleep) right now.'
practiceQuestions.answer: The baby is sleeping right now.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The present continuous is used for actions happening at the moment of speaking.

practiceQuestions.question: Translate to English: 'Eu estou evitando contato com ele.'
practiceQuestions.answer: I am avoiding contact with him.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Present continuous is used to express an ongoing action.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking cultures, punctuality is highly valued, especially in professional settings.
The use of 'daily routines' is common in conversations about work and lifestyle.
studyTips: Practice forming sentences in the present continuous to describe your daily actions.
Use flashcards to memorize new vocabulary and their translations.
originalExamples: Don't ask me to sit next to Noah. I'm avoiding contact with him. (Não me peça para sentar ao lado de Noah. Estou evitando contato com ele.)
I can't participate in the project. I'm finishing another campaign. (Não posso participar do projeto. Estou terminando outra campanha.)
Please don't make so much noise. I'm studying. The baby is sleeping. (Por favor, não faça tanto barulho. Estou estudando. O bebê está dormindo.)
I need to eat something soon. I'm eating every three hours. I'm getting hungry. (Preciso comer algo em breve. Estou comendo a cada três horas. Estou ficando com fome.)
I don't have anywhere to live now. I'm travelling all the time / around the world. (Não tenho onde morar agora. Estou viajando o tempo todo / pelo mundo.)
We need to go to the supermarket. I'm cooking the last piece of meat. (Precisamos ir ao supermercado. Estou cozinhando o último pedaço de carne.)
They don't need their car any more. They're living near to the subway. (Eles não precisam mais do carro. Eles estão morando perto do metrô.)
Things are not so good at work. I'm selling below the target. (As coisas não estão tão boas no trabalho. Estou vendendo abaixo da meta.)
It isn't true what he said. He's lying about his work. (Não é verdade o que ele disse. Ele está mentindo sobre seu trabalho.)
We're going to get wet if we go out now. It's raining now. (Vamos nos molhar se sairmos agora. Está chovendo agora.)

My husband and I are in contact with the orphanage. We're talking with social worker. We're looking for a child for adoption. (Meu marido e eu estamos em contato com o orfanato. Estamos conversando com a assistente social. Estamos procurando uma criança para adoção.)
I want to lose weight. I'm working on this. (Quero perder peso. Estou trabalhando nisso.)
